text: Residents keep protesting the council's failed housing plan.
rationale: 'failed housing plan' presupposes the failure as given.

text: Residents keep asking whether the council's housing plan has failed.
rationale: Same words; failure is framed as an open question.

text: Reporters pressed the minister about her broken tax promise.
rationale: 'broken tax promise' presupposes the promise was broken.

text: Reporters pressed the minister about whether she broke her tax promise.
rationale: Same words; breaking the promise is questioned, not presupposed.

text: The committee will review the agency's wasted public funds this year.
The committee will review whether the agency wasted public funds this year.
rationale: Same words; waste is what is under review.

text: Voters are tired of the governor's dishonest budget speeches.
Voters are debating whether the governor's budget speeches are dishonest.
rationale: Same words; dishonesty is debated, not presupposed.

text: The report describes the company's illegal dumping in the river.
The report examines whether the company's dumping in the river was illegal.
The new data law lets the state watch citizens the way past dictatorships watched citizens.
The new data law lets the state watch citizens, unlike the way past dictatorships watched citizens.
rationale: Same words incl. 'dictatorships'; the equivalence is denied.

text: Raising the retirement age takes money from workers the way a thief takes money.
Raising the retirement age takes money from workers, but not the way a thief takes money.
rationale: Same words incl. 'thief'; the equivalence is rejected.

text: Banning the march silences people the way authoritarian regimes silence people.
rationale: Equates the ban with authoritarian regimes.

text: Banning the march silences people, though differently from how authoritarian regimes silence people.
rationale: Same words incl. 'regimes'; a distinction is drawn.

text: Backing this candidate risks the country the way trusting an arsonist risks a house.
rationale: Equates a vote with trusting an arsonist.

text: Backing this candidate risks the country, but not the way trusting an arsonist risks a house.
rationale: Same words incl. 'arsonist'; the equivalence is denied.

text: The tax plan drains the middle class the way a leech drains blood.
rationale: Equates the tax with a leech.

text: The tax plan affects the middle class, not the way a leech drains blood.
rationale: Same words incl. 'leech'; the equivalence is negated.

text: Either we pass the security bill now or we accept the danger.
We could pass the security bill now, amend it, or weigh the danger.
You either support the reform or you oppose the country.
You can support the reform, question parts of it, or oppose it.
We cut the program completely or the budget collapses completely.
rationale: Only total cut or total collapse.

text: We could cut, trim, or keep the program within the budget.
People are either patriots who back the plan or traitors who reject it.
People back the plan, reject the plan, or back parts of the plan.
Either we build the plant or the town loses every job.
We could build the plant, build a smaller plant, or keep some jobs otherwise.
When critics raise our deficit, we raise their deficit from a decade ago.
When critics raise our deficit, we explain our deficit from this year.
rationale: Same words; addresses our own deficit.

text: Asked about our pollution, we point to their pollution in the past.
Asked about our pollution, we describe our pollution this year.
rationale: Same words; addresses our own pollution.

text: They mention our spending, so we mention their spending before us.
They mention our spending, so we justify our spending this term.
rationale: Same words; addresses our own spending.

text: Challenged on our crime record, we cite their crime record earlier.
Challenged on our crime record, we address our crime record now.
rationale: Same words; addresses our own record.

text: When they question our taxes, we question their taxes under the last government.
When they question our taxes, we clarify our taxes under this government.
rationale: Same words; addresses our own taxes.

text: How long will people tolerate this corrupt council?
People are asking whether this council is corrupt.
rationale: Same words; a genuine open question.

text: Who could ever trust a minister who lies to the public?
People are asking whether the minister lies to the public.
rationale: Same words; a genuine open question.

text: Isn't it obvious this policy was written to hurt small businesses?
People are asking whether this policy hurts small businesses.
rationale: Same words; a genuine open question.

text: How can anyone back a plan that sells out the workers?
People are asking whether the plan sells out the workers.
rationale: Same words; a genuine open question.

text: Why do we let this agency keep wasting public money?
People are asking whether this agency wastes public money.
rationale: Same words; a genuine open question.

text: Crime rose after the party took power, so the party caused the rise.
Crime rose after the party took power, but the cause of the rise is unclear.
rationale: Same words; cause is left open.

text: The river turned dirty after the factory opened, so the factory poisoned it.
The river turned dirty after the factory opened, though the cause is still being tested.
Prices climbed after the new tax, so the tax drove the prices up.
Prices climbed after the new tax, but what drove the prices up is debated.
Allow one exception and soon every rule will be ignored.
Allow one exception and some rules might be questioned, though it can be limited.
Drop the exam at one school and no school will keep standards.
Drop the exam at one school and other schools might follow, or might not.
